findings.text: You must submit your app for review if you want to make it available to users in any Asana workspace beyond your own or list it publicly.
findings.quote: Submitting your app for review is not required to obtain a token. You only need to submit your app if you intend to: Make your app available to users in any Asana workspace, beyond your own organization or development environment List your app publicly on the Asana app directory

findings.text: The initial response time for app submissions is aimed to be within one week.
findings.quote: We aim to provide an initial response on app submissions within one week. However, the review timeline may vary depending on the complexity of the app.

findings.text: Navigate to the developer console to select Submit for review in the sidebar.
findings.quote: When managing your app in the developer console, select Submit for review in the sidebar to access the app submission form:

findings.text: Complete the pre-flight checklist of app features in the developer console.
findings.quote: From there, you'll review an interactive "pre-flight" checklist of app features before submitting an app.

findings.text: Select the Publish app button in the developer console after your submission passes requirements.
findings.quote: At this point, you can select the Publish app button in the developer console to share your app:

findings.text: Perform a self-QA review before submitting your app for review.
findings.quote: Before submitting your app for review, we recommend that you perform a self-QA review by thoroughly testing your app experiences, marketing copy, authorization, and security best practices.

findings.text: Apps cannot be edited once they have been submitted for review.
findings.quote: Once your app has been submitted on the Submit for review page, the review process will begin. At this point, the app will no longer be open for further edits.

findings.quote: If the state does not match, your app should return a 422 error.

findings.quote: If the computed signature and x-asana-request-signature do not match, your app server should return a 400 error.

findings.quote: Your app server should check this value and only return a 200 response if the current date and time is before the expires_at time.

findings.text: You must register your application with Asana to receive a client ID and client secret.
findings.quote: You must first register your application with Asana to receive a client ID and client secret. To do so, first visit the developer console and select Create new app, as shown below:

findings.text: Visit the developer console and select Create new app.
findings.quote: To do so, first visit the developer console and select Create new app, as shown below:

findings.text: Supply your new application with an app name.
findings.quote: App name - The name for your application. Users will see this name when your application requests permission to access their account as well as when they review the list of apps they have authorized.

findings.text: Do not share your client secret or include it in source code.
findings.quote: Your client secret is a secret, and it should never be shared with anyone or added into source code that others could gain access to.

findings.text: Requests without PKCE parameters will be rejected for localhost, 127.0.0.1, or native URN redirect URIs.
findings.quote: OAuth flows that use a localhost, 127.0.0.1, or native URN redirect URI must use PKCE (S256). Include a code_challenge in the authorization request and the matching code_verifier in the token exchange. Requests without these parameters will be rejected.

findings.text: Asana recommends using a library to handle OAuth details.
findings.quote: We recommend using a library (available in your language of choice) to handle the details of OAuth. Along with expediting development time, using a library can help mitigate the risk of security vulnerabilities due to inexperience or oversight.

findings.text: Using scopes is strongly recommended.
findings.quote: Using scopes is strongly recommended, however, scopes are not yet available for every Asana API endpoint.

findings.text: Asana recommends using OAuth for apps intended for any user to discover.
findings.quote: If you are building an app for any user to discover, we recommend creating an app and using OAuth.
